items.title: [Bug]: Agent can destroy its own runtime venv by running 'uv venv' via terminal tool

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

The terminal tool permits the agent to run `uv venv <path>` with `<path>` resolving to the agent's own running venv. When this happens, `uv venv` silently replaces the live venv with an empty one mid-session, stripping every installed package including `certifi`. The next LLM API call then fails with `FileNotFoundError [Errno 2]: No such file or directory` from httpx's CA bundle lookup, and the agent dies.

This is fully reproducible when the agent tries to install an additional editable package into its own environment and falls through the `uv pip install` → `uv pip install --system` → `uv venv` ladder. The last rung nukes the runtime.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes via the method in CONTRIBUTING.md (`uv venv venv --python 3.11 && uv pip install -e ".[all,dev]"`). The project-local `venv/` becomes the agent's running runtime.
2. Start `hermes chat` and ask the agent to install an additional editable package into its environment (e.g., an optional submodule package).
3. The agent tries `uv pip install -e ./some-pkg` — fails with "no pip in venv".
4. Retries `uv pip install --system -e ./some-pkg` — blocked by PEP 668.
5. Falls back to "I will create a new environment": `uv venv venv` from the project directory.
6. `uv venv` replaces the existing `venv/` with an empty one. The running Python process loses its site-packages silently.
7. Next LLM API call fails: `FileNotFoundError [Errno 2]` on `.../certifi/cacert.pem`. Agent dies.

## Expected Behavior

The terminal tool should treat any command whose target resolves to the agent's running runtime (`sys.prefix`) as dangerous and require explicit user approval, matching the existing self-termination protection (`pkill hermes`, `kill $(pgrep hermes)`).

## Actual Behavior

`uv venv venv`, `python -m venv venv`, and `rm -rf venv/` against the runtime all execute silently and kill the running agent.

## Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

0.8.0 (build 2026.4.8)

## Relevant Logs / Traceback

```
API call failed (attempt 1/3): FileNotFoundError
  Provider: custom  Model: <redacted>
  Endpoint: http://<redacted>:8000/v1
  Error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
Retrying in 2.74s (attempt 1/3)...
[...]
API failed after 3 retries - [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

The `FileNotFoundError` traces to httpx → certifi loading `cacert.pem` from `<venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/certifi/`, which was removed when `uv venv` recreated the directory.

## Root Cause Analysis

Two converging factors:

1. **`uv venv` silently replaces existing directories.** Before astral-sh/uv#14309 (merged 2025-07-16), `uv venv <path>` removed an existing directory at the target and recreated it without warning. Some invocation paths can still reach this behavior. See astral-sh/uv#1472 and astral-sh/uv#4276 for history.

2. **Hermes venv has no `pip`.** Same root cause as #7309. When the agent is asked to install a package and the venv lacks `pip`, it falls through to `uv pip install --system` (blocked by PEP 668) and then to `uv venv`, which is the sequence that triggers the self-clobber.

`tools/approval.py` already protects against self-termination (`pkill hermes`, `kill $(pgrep hermes)`) but not against self-mutation of the Python environment, even though the outcome is the same.

## Proposed Fix

Extend `tools/approval.py` with a structural check (not regex-based) that parses commands with `shlex.split`, extracts target paths from known venv-creating commands (`uv venv`, `python -m venv`, `virtualenv`) and `rm -rf`, resolves them against cwd, and flags the command when the target lies inside `sys.prefix`. This fits alongside the existing self-termination patterns and requires user approval for the dangerous subset without blocking legitimate uses of these commands against unrelated paths.

PR implementing this fix: will be linked as soon as I open it.

Related: #7309 (same underlying cause — venv ships without `pip`, forcing the agent into fragile fallback paths).

items.title: [Bug]: Cron inactivity timeout fires during active openai-codex streaming because Codex stream events do not update activity tracker

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Opening this on behalf of Yann Bonzom after reproducing it in real cron usage.

Cron jobs using `openai-codex` / Codex Responses can be killed by the cron inactivity timeout even while the provider is actively streaming reasoning/text.

Example error:

`TimeoutError: Cron job '<job-name>' idle for 1850s (limit 1800s) — last activity: starting API call #1`

## Environment

- Hermes Agent
- Provider: `openai-codex`
- Model: `gpt-5.4`
- Cron timeout: `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT=1800`

## Root cause

The Codex Responses streaming path does not keep the activity tracker fresh while stream events are arriving.

Affected paths in `run_agent.py`:
- `_run_codex_stream(...)`
- `_run_codex_create_stream_fallback(...)`

Cron relies on `agent.get_activity_summary()` / `_touch_activity()` to determine whether a run is actually idle. In the Codex stream path, the last activity can remain stuck at `starting API call #N` even though stream events are still flowing.

## Why this is a distinct bug

This is related to the broader inactivity-timeout family (#4815, #6260, #6582), but it is a separate issue:
- not the original wall-clock timeout problem
- not the delegation child-activity propagation problem
- specifically missing `_touch_activity()` updates inside Codex Responses stream handling

## Reproduction pattern

1. Run a cron job on `openai-codex` / Codex Responses
2. Let it hit a response that streams for a while
3. Observe cron failure with stale activity text like `last activity: starting API call #1`
4. Cron kills the job after the inactivity limit even though the provider was likely still actively streaming/reasoning

## Proposed fix

Update activity tracking during Codex Responses streaming by calling `_touch_activity()`:
- when entering the stream wait
- on each stream event
- on text deltas
- on reasoning deltas
- in the `create(stream=True)` fallback path as well

## Local validation

I validated a local fix with a regression test that asserts Codex stream events update the activity tracker.

Passing tests:
- `python -m pytest tests/run_agent/test_streaming.py -q`
- `python -m pytest tests/cron/test_cron_inactivity_timeout.py -q`

## Note

I also saw one timeout with `last activity: API call #1 completed`, which may indicate a secondary idle path worth checking after API completion. But the main reproducible bug here is the missing activity updates during Codex stream handling.

items.title: [Bug]: smart_model_routing triggers preflight compression against the cheap model's threshold

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When `smart_model_routing` routes a turn to the cheap model, CLI rebuilds the `AIAgent`, which creates a new `ContextCompressor` bound to the cheap model's `context_length`. Preflight compression then compares the current request size against that cheap-model threshold. If the cheap model has a smaller context window than the primary, a long-running session can hit the cheap threshold even when the user sent a trivial message, and the session history gets compressed on that turn.

The impact is that `self.conversation_history` in the CLI is overwritten with the compressed version, the active session transitions to a new child session in SQLite, and the user sees only the short reply from the cheap model without realizing anything happened. The original session is still reachable through `hermes sessions browse` because `_compress_context()` creates the child session with `parent_id` pointing to the original, but the active session from that point forward is the compressed one.

Triggering conditions (50% threshold, `threshold_percent=0.50`):

| Primary model | Cheap model | Primary threshold | Cheap threshold | Fires when history > |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude-sonnet-4.6 (1M) | gemini-2.5-flash (1M) | 500K | 500K | never (default config — safe) |
| claude-sonnet-4.6 (1M) | gpt-4o-mini (128K) | 500K | 64K | ~64K tokens |
| claude-sonnet-4.6 (1M) | claude-haiku-4.5 (200K) | 500K | 100K | ~100K tokens |
| qwen3.6-plus (131K) | smaller cheap | 65K | proportional | proportional |

The default cheap model (`gemini-2.5-flash`, 1M) hides this bug from most users. Anyone who intuitively sets cheap to a "smaller, cheaper" model is exposed.

## Steps to Reproduce

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
model:
  default: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6   # ~1M context
  provider: openrouter

smart_model_routing:
  enabled: true
  max_simple_chars: 160
  max_simple_words: 28
  cheap_model:
    provider: openrouter
    model: openai/gpt-4o-mini            # ~128K context
```

1. `hermes chat`
2. Have a conversation that accumulates ~80K tokens of history (above gpt-4o-mini's 64K threshold, well under Sonnet's 500K)
3. Send a short message like `hi`
4. Smart routing picks `gpt-4o-mini`; preflight compression runs on this turn

## Expected Behavior

The cheap model handles one short turn. Session history stays intact. Compression decisions stay anchored to the primary model's context budget, since that's the model the session was sized for.

## Actual Behavior

On the cheap-routed turn:

- `AIAgent` is torn down and rebuilt (`cli.py:7081-7083`)
- New `ContextCompressor` uses gpt-4o-mini's `context_length=128K`, `threshold_tokens=64K`
- Preflight hits the threshold, `_compress_context()` runs
- `self.conversation_history` is replaced with the compressed version (`cli.py:6735`)
- A new child session is created in SQLite with `parent_id` pointing to the original

## Affected Component

- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
- CLI (interactive chat)

## Operating System

macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0)

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

v0.8.0 (2026.4.8), commit `af9caec4`

## Relevant Logs / Traceback

No traceback — the bug runs through the happy path. Logs at INFO level show:

```
Preflight compression: ~80,123 tokens >= 64,000 threshold (model openai/gpt-4o-mini, ctx 128000)
context compression started: session=... messages=120 tokens=~80,123 model=openai/gpt-4o-mini
context compression done: session=... messages=120->35 tokens=~28,500
```

## Root Cause Analysis

Call chain on `af9caec4`:

1. `cli.py:7081-7083` — every turn, `_resolve_turn_agent_config()` returns a new route signature; if it differs from the previous turn, `self.agent = None`.
2. `cli.py:7088` → `cli.py:2757 _init_agent(model_override=..., runtime_override=...)` creates a fresh `AIAgent` with the cheap model.
3. `run_agent.py:1314-1326` — `AIAgent.__init__` constructs `ContextCompressor(model=self.model, ...)` where `self.model` is now the cheap model. This path runs whenever no plugin context engine is selected (the default).
4. `agent/context_compressor.py:116-124` — `self.context_length = get_model_context_length(model, ...)` and `self.threshold_tokens = int(self.context_length * threshold_percent)` resolve against the cheap model.
5. `run_agent.py:7578-7584` — preflight:
   ```python
   _preflight_tokens = estimate_request_tokens_rough(
       messages,
       system_prompt=active_system_prompt or "",
       tools=self.tools or None,
   )
   if _preflight_tokens >= self.context_compressor.threshold_tokens:
       # compress up to 3 passes
   ```
6. `run_agent.py:7599-7620` — compression runs, clears `conversation_history = None` (the #7001 fix), creates a new child session.
7. `cli.py:6735` — CLI overwrites `self.conversation_history` with `result["messages"]`.

The core issue: step 3 rebinds the compressor to the temporary model, but smart routing is a per-turn override. Compression decisions should stay anchored to the primary model.

Two notes specific to v0.8.0:

- `estimate_request_tokens_rough` now includes tool schemas in the estimate. The inline comment notes this can add 20–30K tokens. Users upgrading from v0.7.x may cross thresholds they didn't hit before.
- PR #7001 (commit `871313ae`) added `conversation_history = None` after mid-loop compression. That prevents the new session from being empty in SQLite, but doesn't prevent the compression from firing in the first place, so it's orthogonal to this bug.

## Proposed Fix

Three options, smallest first:

**A. Skip preflight compression on smart-routed turns (~10 LOC)**

Mark the turn as temporary-routed in `cli.py:chat()` before calling `_init_agent`, and skip the preflight check in `run_conversation`. If the cheap model itself can't accept the request, the existing in-loop compression on API error still catches it.

```python
# cli.py — after _init_agent returns
self.agent._skip_preflight_for_turn = bool(turn_route.get("label"))
```

```python
# run_agent.py:7584 — before the preflight branch
_skip_preflight = getattr(self, "_skip_preflight_for_turn", False)
self._skip_preflight_for_turn = False  # one-shot
if not _skip_preflight and _preflight_tokens >= self.context_compressor.threshold_tokens:
    ...
```

**B. Anchor preflight threshold to the primary model**

Pass the primary model's `context_length` as a separate `threshold_context_length_override` when the compressor is built during a smart-routing rebuild. Preflight uses the override; `compress()` uses the active model's real context for API sizing.

This fits the new `ContextEngine` ABC (`agent/context_engine.py`) — the interface already has `should_compress_preflight()` as an extension point. More invasive than A but cleaner long-term.

**C. Make smart routing a per-call override, not an agent rebuild**

Instead of setting `self.agent = None` on signature change, do an in-place swap of `self.model`/`self.client`/`self.base_url`/`self.api_key` for one API call and restore at the next turn. The infrastructure already exists for 429 fallback:

- `_try_activate_fallback()` at `run_agent.py:5202-5251`
- `_restore_primary_runtime()` at `run_agent.py:5343-5392`

Smart routing could reuse the same mechanism. Side effect: #4568 (status bar showing wrong model during smart routing) goes away because the agent's canonical model is never changed.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — I can put up a PR for fix **A** as a starting point, and a separate discussion / follow-up for **C** if maintainers think the refactor is worth it.

## Related Issues

- #4568 (open) — CLI chat status-bar shows stale model during smart routing. Same root cause (smart routing mutates agent state).
- #6844 (closed, fix `fd3e855d`) — preserves `config_context_length` on `/model` switch. That fix is on the `switch_model()` path, which is separate from the smart-routing destroy-and-rebuild path, so it doesn't cover this bug.
- #7001 (closed, commit `871313ae`) — clears `conversation_history` after mid-loop compression. Partially mitigates symptoms but not the root cause.

## Summary
The current OpenAI Codex auth integration is fundamentally broken when Hermes imports or syncs credentials from `~/.codex/auth.json`.

Hermes uses the shared Codex `refresh_token` to refresh its own session. Because those refresh tokens are single-use / rotating, once Hermes consumes the token, the other client that was sharing the same auth state (for example Codex CLI or VS Code) can no longer use it.

In plain English: Hermes is effectively stealing the other client's refresh token turn. That implementation is too dumb for a shared auth file.

## Why this is a bug
- Hermes explicitly reads and syncs tokens from `~/.codex/auth.json`.
- Hermes then calls the refresh-token flow itself.
- Codex refresh tokens are single-use / rotated.
- Result: after Hermes refreshes, the other client can hit `refresh_token_reused`, stale-token, or logged-out behavior.

The code already seems aware this race exists because it contains logic/comments about:
- syncing from `~/.codex/auth.json` before refresh
- avoiding `refresh_token_reused`
- retrying if another client already consumed the token

That means this is not theoretical — the implementation is built around an auth conflict that should not exist in the first place.

## Expected behavior
Hermes should not participate in refresh-token rotation for credentials sourced from the shared Codex auth file.

At minimum, one of these should happen:
1. Do not import / sync `refresh_token` from `~/.codex/auth.json` at all.
2. Treat imported Codex CLI credentials as read-only and never refresh them from Hermes.
3. Force users through a fully independent Hermes-owned auth flow before using `openai-codex`.
4. Refuse to use shared Codex CLI auth if Hermes cannot guarantee non-interference.

## Actual behavior
Hermes can consume the shared refresh token, which makes the other client unable to use it.

## Suggested fix direction
The safest fix is to stop sharing refresh-token state with Codex CLI entirely:
- use Hermes-owned auth only, or
- treat `~/.codex/auth.json` as migration input / read-only bootstrap, never as a live shared token source.

## Context
I'm filing this because the current behavior causes real client interference: one app refreshes, the other app breaks.

items.title: Bug: checkpoint_manager.py fails with FileNotFoundError when working_dir contains unexpanded tilde (~)
items.body:
## Bug Description

`tools/checkpoint_manager.py` uses `Path(working_dir).resolve()` in 8 places to normalize directory paths. However, `Path.resolve()` does **not** expand `~` — only `Path.expanduser()` does.

When a working directory is passed as a string containing `~` (e.g. `~/.hermes`, `~/.config/x-cli`), `resolve()` treats `~` as a literal directory name relative to CWD, producing paths like `/root/~/.hermes` instead of `/root/.hermes`.

This causes `FileNotFoundError` in `subprocess.run()` since the `cwd` parameter points to a non-existent directory.

## Error Log

```
ERROR tools.checkpoint_manager: Git executable not found: git init
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tools/checkpoint_manager.py", line 107, in _run_git
    result = subprocess.run(...)
  ...
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/root/~/.hermes'
```

The error message says "Git executable not found" but the actual cause is the invalid `cwd` path — git is installed and on PATH.

## Fix

Add `.expanduser()` before `.resolve()` in all 8 occurrences in `tools/checkpoint_manager.py`:

```diff
# _shadow_repo_path()
- abs_path = str(Path(working_dir).resolve())
+ abs_path = str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve())

# _git_env()
- env["GIT_WORK_TREE"] = str(Path(working_dir).resolve())
+ env["GIT_WORK_TREE"] = str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve())

# _run_git()
- cwd=str(Path(working_dir).resolve()),
+ cwd=str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve()),

# _init_shadow_repo()
- str(Path(working_dir).resolve()) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
+ str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve()) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"

# ensure_checkpoint()
- abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).resolve())
+ abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve())

# list_checkpoints()
- abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).resolve())
+ abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve())

# diff()
- abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).resolve())
+ abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve())

# restore()
- abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).resolve())
+ abs_dir = str(Path(working_dir).expanduser().resolve())

# get_working_dir_for_path()
- path = Path(file_path).resolve()
+ path = Path(file_path).expanduser().resolve()
```

## Environment
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux x86_64)
- Python: 3.11.15
- Running via gateway (`hermes gateway run`)
- Triggered during checkpoint auto-save when the agent edits files in `~/.hermes/` or `~/.config/` paths

items.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — usage metadata, staleness, archival, and revalidation
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

Hermes has a strong self-improvement loop for skills (`create` / `edit` / `patch`), but it does not have an equivalent forgetting / retirement loop.

Today, skills mostly grow monotonically. Over time this creates several problems:

- stale or environment-specific guidance can persist after conditions change (related: #6051)
- repeated patching can accumulate drift, conflicting instructions, or over-generalization
- rarely used long-tail skills remain equally visible in the catalog / prompt path, adding overhead (related: #2045)
- there is no principled way to distinguish “rare but important” skills from genuinely obsolete ones

Issue #429 already raises the question of whether Hermes should track skill usage timestamps / counters. This issue proposes turning that into a concrete lifecycle system.

Related: #6051, #429, #1780, #2045, #416

## Proposed Solution

Introduce a lightweight lifecycle layer for skills, separate from the SKILL.md content itself.

### 1. Add sidecar lifecycle metadata

Track operational metadata outside the skill file (for example in a small JSON/SQLite sidecar index keyed by skill path/name), such as:

- `last_viewed_at` (weak signal)
- `last_used_at` or `last_successful_apply_at` (stronger signal)
- `use_count`
- `patch_count`
- `last_patched_at`
- `pinned`
- `archived_at`
- optional: `negative_claim_confidence` / `negative_claim_ttl`

I would strongly prefer sidecar metadata over rewriting frontmatter on every use:

- less noisy than mutating SKILL.md constantly
- avoids polluting user-authored content
- reduces conflict pressure for bundled / hub / externally updated skills (related to #1780)

### 2. Add lifecycle states

Introduce simple states such as:

- `active` — normal behavior, visible for prompt/catalog use
- `stale` — not recently used; hidden from default prompt injection or deprioritized
- `archived` — excluded by default but recoverable

Important: I would **not** auto-delete by default. Archival is much safer than deletion.

### 3. Filter or deprioritize stale skills in prompt construction

When Hermes builds the skills prompt/catalog, stale or archived skills should not be treated the same as active ones.

This helps with:

- reducing prompt clutter from long-tail skills
- lowering the chance that stale guidance keeps influencing the agent
- preserving recovery paths for rarely needed but still useful skills

A pinned skill should remain active regardless of recency.

### 4. Revalidate negative / environment-dependent claims

A special case is skills that encode negative operational claims such as:

- “browser tools do not work”
- “X command is unavailable”
- “Y setup never succeeds”

These claims are often environment-dependent and may become false later.

For these, Hermes should support a TTL / revalidation mechanism instead of treating them as permanent truths. This directly addresses the failure mode in #6051.

### 5. Recovery path

Archived or stale skills should be easy to revive:

- explicit user request
- successful reuse
- manual unarchive command
- optional background review that suggests reactivation

### 6. Configurability

Possible config surface:

```yaml
skills:
  lifecycle:
    enabled: true
    stale_after_days: 30
    archive_after_days: 90
    revalidate_negative_claims: true
    negative_claim_ttl_days: 14
    hide_stale_from_prompt: true
```

## Alternatives Considered

### Pure recency/frequency scoring only

Cheap and easy, but too blunt. Some skills are low-frequency but high-value. A `pinned` mechanism is needed.

### Automatic hard deletion

Too risky. Skills should probably move through `active -> stale -> archived` first, with deletion as an explicit/manual action.

### Store counters directly in frontmatter

Simple, but noisy and conflict-prone. It also mixes operational telemetry with human-authored skill content.

### Manual cleanup only

This is effectively the current behavior, and it does not scale well as the number of learned skills grows.

## Why this matters

Hermes’ self-improvement loop is one of its strongest differentiators. But a learning system that only accumulates and never forgets will eventually collect stale heuristics, prompt clutter, and brittle generalizations.

Memory already has concepts like decay / forgetting. Skills likely need an equivalent lifecycle layer.

## Feature Type

Performance / reliability

## Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor)

## Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Two architectural gaps exposed by a launchctl self-kill loop: smart approval auto-approves self-termination, and resume doesn't detect post-crash retry
items.body:
While diagnosing a self-kill loop in an `ade` profile on macOS (2026-04-11,
~14 hours of a codex model repeatedly running `launchctl kickstart -k gui/
$(id -u)/ai.hermes.gateway-ade` and getting SIGTERMed, then being resumed),
I found two architectural gaps that are independent of the specific
`launchctl` pattern and are worth discussing separately from a
pattern-blocklist fix.

Raising as one issue because they showed up in the same incident and interact;
happy to split into two if preferred.

I also have a [PR linked above](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/7817) for the pattern-level part (launchctl and
hermes CLI patterns). This issue is about the two *architectural* gaps that a
pattern fix alone does not address.

---

### (A) Smart approval auto-approves self-termination commands

#### What happened

With `approvals.mode: smart`, the incident command hit `DANGEROUS_PATTERNS`
(after my local patch added `launchctl kickstart`). `_smart_approve` called
the auxiliary LLM and got back `APPROVE`. The command ran anyway, with this
tool result annotation:

```json
{
  "output": "Background process started",
  "pid": 66524,
  "exit_code": 0,
  "approval": "Command was flagged (macOS launchctl service control
               (self-termination risk)) and auto-approved by smart approval."
}
```

#### Why

The [smart approval prompt at `tools/approval.py:541`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/af9caec4/tools/approval.py#L541)
asks the auxiliary LLM to classify commands along a spectrum from "harmless
false positive" (e.g. `python -c "print('hello')"`) to "genuinely damaging"
(e.g. `mkfs`, fork bombs, `DROP TABLE`). The prompt examples all describe
classic destructive operations on data or system state.

There's no mental model in the prompt for **self-termination** — "this
command would kill the process that's asking me to evaluate it." From the
auxiliary LLM's perspective, `launchctl kickstart -k ai.hermes.gateway-ade`
looks like routine service management, not obviously destructive. The LLM
cannot know that the caller *is* the service, because the self-targeting
context isn't in the command text.

The `pattern_key` passed to the LLM does mention `"self-termination risk"` in
the description, but it's buried at the end of a formatted string and the
prompt doesn't explicitly tell the LLM to hard-deny anything in the
self-termination class.

#### Observation: smart approval is MORE dangerous than manual for this class

Counterintuitively, `mode: manual` is safer for profiles that might self-manage.
In manual mode the command would hit the Discord-side `/approve` `/deny`
prompt, the gateway would block, and the human would have a chance to notice.
In smart mode the LLM routinely auto-approves and the gateway dies before any
human sees the prompt.

#### Suggested fix

Introduce a "never auto-approve" tag on patterns that represent self-harm
classes (self-termination, session corruption, secret exfiltration, etc.).
The smart approval path should treat these patterns as `escalate` regardless
of the auxiliary LLM's opinion, routing to the human via gateway queue or CLI
prompt.

Rough shape:

```python
DANGEROUS_PATTERNS = [
    (r'\brm\s+(-[^\s]*\s+)*/', "delete in root path",
     flags=PatternFlags.DEFAULT),
    ...
    (r'\blaunchctl\s+(kickstart|kill|bootout|bootstrap)\b',
     "macOS launchctl service control (self-termination risk)",
     flags=PatternFlags.NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE),
    ...
]
```

Or simpler: a module-level set `_NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE_KEYS = {...}` checked in
`_smart_approve` before the LLM call:

```python
def _smart_approve(command, description, pattern_keys):
    if _NEVER_AUTO_APPROVE_KEYS & set(pattern_keys):
        return "escalate"
    # ... existing LLM call
```

A stronger prompt update (explicitly telling the LLM "never approve
self-termination") would help but is less robust than a pure code gate.

---

### (B) Resume does not detect post-crash retry of dangerous tool calls

#### What happened

On each gateway restart, the new gateway loaded the session from
`state.db`. The last messages looked like:

```
[assistant tool_call]  launchctl kickstart -k ai.hermes.gateway-ade ; ...
[tool result]          {"output": "[Command interrupted — user sent a new
                        message]", "exit_code": 130}
```

The codex model, seeing its own tool call followed by a 130 exit, reasonably
interpreted this as "my last attempt was interrupted, I should try again" and
re-emitted the same command. Plus any new user messages arriving during the
loop got interleaved as additional context, which the model absorbed into the
same plan.

#### Why

There's no resume-time inspection of the tail of the session for the
specific pattern "assistant called a dangerous tool, tool returned exit 130,
session was then truncated and restarted by launchd/systemd." This pattern is
specific enough to detect: (a) last non-user message is an interrupted tool
result, (b) the corresponding tool call matched `DANGEROUS_PATTERNS`, (c) the
gateway restart is visible in logs.

#### Suggested fix

At session load time (or during the first run_conversation iteration after
resume), scan the last N messages for this pattern. If detected:

1. Rewrite the tool result content to say something unambiguous like
   `[Tool call was interrupted by gateway restart. The command matched
    DANGEROUS_PATTERNS (description). This is likely a self-termination loop
    — do NOT retry.]`
2. Optionally insert a synthetic system/user message breaking the plan:
   `[System intervention: gateway detected a potential self-termination loop.
    Command has been removed from your retry queue.]`

The first change is minimal and non-invasive — it only rewrites the *tool
result* the model sees, not the tool call itself. The second is a firmer
circuit breaker.

Either is better than the current behavior, where the model sees an
"interrupted" marker and rationally concludes the command should be retried.

---

### (C) Optional: CLAUDE.md / agent system prompt guidance

Lower priority, but worth mentioning: the default system prompt for agent
models doesn't include guidance like "never restart your own gateway from
within a tool call; ask the user to do it externally if needed." For
self-managing profiles (codex, subagent-enabled), this would be a cheap
belt-and-suspenders layer that doesn't require code changes.

---

### Repro / environment

- hermes-agent `af9caec4` (at time of writing) + a local patch adding
  `launchctl kickstart` to `DANGEROUS_PATTERNS` (the PR linked above)
- macOS 14, launchd-managed gateway
- Profile: `ade`, provider `openai-codex`, model `gpt-5.4`
- `approvals.mode: smart` at incident time
- Session DB: `~/.hermes/profiles/ade/state.db`

Command:
```bash
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/ai.hermes.gateway-ade
```

Ran every ~20 seconds for ~14 hours until manually intervened. Smart approval
auto-approved every invocation with:

> "Command was flagged (macOS launchctl service control (self-termination
> risk)) and auto-approved by smart approval."

---

### Why raise this as an issue rather than a PR

Both (A) and (B) are architectural changes I'd prefer to discuss before
implementing. (A) requires agreeing on a pattern-flagging mechanism or a
hard-deny set. (B) touches the resume path and has implications for sessions
that legitimately want to retry interrupted commands. Happy to open PRs for
either after discussion.

The pattern-level fix for the symptom is in a separate PR (linked).

items.title: Session search broad FTS query can fail on hyphenated OR terms
items.body:
## Summary
A broad session-search FTS query can fail when one of the OR terms is hyphenated.

Example query:
- `错题本 OR 错题 OR wrong-book OR mistakes`

Observed failure on SQLite FTS5:
- `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: book`

## Why this happens
SQLite FTS5 can parse a bare hyphenated token like `wrong-book` as a column-filter expression instead of a plain search term. In a broad OR query, that makes the full MATCH expression fail instead of returning results.

## Expected behavior
Broad session-search queries containing ordinary hyphenated search terms should still execute and return matching sessions.

## Actual behavior
The MATCH query can fail at execution time, causing session search to miss valid results for the whole query.

## Proposed fix
Keep the fix narrow at the FTS query sanitization layer:
- normalize duplicated boolean operators that may remain after sanitization
- quote dotted/hyphenated tokens so FTS5 treats them as phrases rather than as punctuation-split expressions

## Reproduction sketch
Using the current session-search database path, a raw SQLite FTS5 MATCH on:
- `错题本 OR 错题 OR wrong-book OR mistakes`
can fail with:
- `no such column: book`

## Notes
I opened a companion PR with the minimal sanitization-based fix and regression coverage.

items.title: [Bug] MCP client does not pass environment variables from config.yaml env: block to subprocess

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When configuring an MCP server in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` with environment variables in the `env:` block, the variables are not passed to the subprocess. This causes MCP servers that require API keys (like minimax-coding-plan-mcp) to fail with 'login fail' errors.

## Configuration

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  tokenplan:
    command: /home/openclaw/.local/bin/minimax-coding-plan-mcp
    args: []
    env:
      MINIMAX_API_KEY: sk-...   # API key configured here
      MINIMAX_API_HOST: https://api.minimaxi.com
      MINIMAX_MCP_BASE_PATH: /tmp/minimax_mcp
    timeout: 300
    connect_timeout: 120
```

## Expected Behavior

Environment variables defined in the `env:` block should be passed to the MCP server subprocess.

## Actual Behavior

The subprocess is spawned but the environment variables are not passed, resulting in:

```
Failed to perform VLM analysis: API Error: login fail: Please carry the API secret key in the 'Authorization' field of the request header, please check your API key and API host.
```

## Verification

Using `mcporter call --stdio` with the same executable and same environment variables works correctly:
```bash
MINIMAX_API_KEY="sk-..." MINIMAX_API_HOST="https://api.minimaxi.com" mcporter call --stdio "/home/openclaw/.local/bin/minimax-coding-plan-mcp" understand_image ...
```

This confirms the issue is with Hermes Agent's MCP client not passing env vars to the subprocess, not with the MCP server itself.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: latest (v2026.4.x)
- Python 3.10
- WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04
- MCP server: minimax-coding-plan-mcp (installed via `uv tool install`)

## Logs

```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: Failed to connect to MCP server 'tokenplan' (command=uvx): Connection closed
ERROR tools.mcp_tool: MCP tool tokenplan/understand_image call failed: TimeoutError
```

## Possible Cause

In `tools/mcp_tool.py`, when spawning the MCP subprocess via stdio, the environment variables from the `env:` config block may not be correctly merged with the filtered baseline environment.

items.title: delegate_task can overwrite delegated custom endpoint with parent custom credential pool

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary
`delegate_task` can misroute subagents that target one custom endpoint when the parent agent runs on a different custom endpoint. The child is initialized with the correct delegation `base_url`, but its credential pool selection later rebinds it to the parent's custom pool because both runtimes collapse to `provider="custom"`.

Reported by Hermes Agent.

## Reproduction
1. Configure the main Hermes runtime to use one custom endpoint (for example a Codex-compatible endpoint).
2. Configure `delegation` to use a different custom endpoint and model.
3. Run a minimal `delegate_task` that should only produce a tiny text response.
4. Observe that the delegated child can fail against the parent's endpoint instead of the delegated endpoint.

## Observed Behavior
The child is initially built with the delegated custom endpoint, but before the delegated run starts it receives a credential pool derived from the parent custom runtime. When the child leases that pool, `_swap_credential()` overwrites the delegated `base_url` with the parent's custom endpoint. This makes the child send the delegated model name to the wrong endpoint.

## Expected Behavior
Delegated children using one custom endpoint should never inherit a different custom endpoint's credential pool. Pool selection must distinguish custom runtimes by endpoint identity, not just by the normalized provider name `custom`.

## Code Evidence
- Delegation config is loaded in `tools/delegate_tool.py` via `_load_config()` and `_resolve_delegation_credentials()`.
- Child agents are built in `tools/delegate_tool.py` with the correct delegated `base_url` and `api_mode`.
- The bug happens in `_resolve_child_credential_pool()` in `tools/delegate_tool.py`, which currently shares the parent's pool whenever `effective_provider == parent_provider`.
- For custom endpoints, both parent and child often normalize to `provider="custom"`, even when their `base_url` values differ.
- Later, `_run_single_child()` acquires a lease from that pool and calls `child._swap_credential(...)`, which overwrites the child's `base_url` with the leased pool entry.

## Root Cause
`_resolve_child_credential_pool()` treats all custom runtimes as interchangeable because it compares only the provider string. It does not account for custom endpoint identity. Named custom providers and explicit `delegation.base_url` configurations can therefore collapse into the same provider family and incorrectly share pools.

## Suggested Fix
When the effective provider is `custom`, resolve the pool by the delegated endpoint identity (for example via the custom pool key derived from the delegated `base_url`) instead of sharing the parent pool based only on provider equality. Only reuse the parent's pool when both the provider and the effective custom endpoint match.

items.title: Weixin: multi-part replies can drop trailing chunks while the agent believes all parts were delivered
items.body:
## Summary

When sending a long reply split into numbered parts (e.g. `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3`) over **Weixin (personal WeChat, iLink Bot API)**, the **last segment may never appear** in the client chat. The user only sees the first segments, but the assistant later **asserts that all parts were already sent** (e.g. that all three messages have been sent), which does not match what appears in WeChat.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (gateway + Weixin adapter)
- Personal WeChat via iLink
- `display.streaming: false` in `config.yaml` (non-streaming path); the issue may also relate to streaming/fallback paths on platforms without message edit support

## Steps to reproduce (observed pattern)

1. Ask the bot for a structured answer in multiple numbered parts (e.g. three sections labeled `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3`).
2. In WeChat, confirm that **only some bubbles** arrive (e.g. `1/3` and `2/3` visible).
3. Send a follow-up such as "继续" / "Continue".
4. The bot responds as if **the full sequence was delivered**, e.g. stating that all three parts were already sent, even though **`3/3` is missing** from the chat history on the phone.

## Expected behavior

- Every chunk Hermes intends to send should either **arrive in WeChat** or the user should get an **explicit error / retry**, and the assistant should **not** claim completion if a chunk failed.
- If partial delivery occurs, the next turn should **detect or acknowledge** missing segments (or re-send the missing tail).

## Actual behavior

- **Partial delivery**: later numbered segments sometimes do not show up.
- **State mismatch**: the model/gateway continues as if **all segments succeeded**, so the user sees contradictory messaging ("3 parts sent") vs. the visible thread (only 2 parts).

## Hypothesis (for maintainers)

- iLink / WeChat may **drop, rate-limit, or fail** on subsequent `sendmessage` calls in a tight loop without per-chunk confirmation or backoff.
- Non-streaming path uses chunked `send()` with `MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (~4000); a mid-loop failure might not surface clearly to the user or to the agent's "done" state.
- Streaming path: Weixin does not support `edit_message`; stream consumer fallback / continuation logic might interact badly with `already_sent` and multi-chunk fallbacks (possible silent truncation on later chunks).

## Logs / artifacts

- Please check `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log` around the time of the missing bubble for `iLink POST` / `send failed` / HTTP errors after the first successful chunk.

## Suggested directions

- Add **short delays between Weixin chunks**, **retries with backoff** on failed sends, and **surface errors** to the user when a chunk fails.
- After multi-chunk send, verify **all chunks succeeded** before treating the turn as complete; avoid assistant copy that assumes full delivery unless confirmed.

Thank you.

items.title: [Tracking] hermes claw migrate — known bugs, schema drift, and gaps
items.body:
## Context

`hermes claw migrate` handles persona, memory, user profile, skills, model config, TTS, MCP servers, command allowlists, and messaging platform settings across 30+ categories. The two-layer design (CLI wrapper in `hermes_cli/claw.py` + migration engine in `openclaw_to_hermes.py`) is thorough for the config landscape it was written against.

The problem is that landscape has shifted. OpenClaw has restructured workspace paths, channel config schemas, TTS provider names, provider API type identifiers, and the `thinkingDefault` enum. The migrate tool silently finds nothing at the old locations, skipping data without warning. This is the single most discussed pain point in the community (~180 messages from ~60 users in a two-week window).

This issue tracks all known problems. Each claim has been verified against the current source code and cross-referenced against the current OpenClaw config schema.

---

## PRs Filed

| # | PR | What | Priority | Lines | Status |
|---|-----|------|----------|-------|--------|
| 1 | #7869 | Find files in `workspace-main/` (memories/persona fix) | **P0** | +13 | Open |
| 2 | #7860 | Read API keys from `openclaw.json["env"]` sub-object | **P0** | +15 | Open |
| 3 | #5207 | Copy `openclaw.json` post-migration (pre-existing) | **P0** | ~16 | Open |
| 4 | #7861 | Extract channel tokens from `accounts.default.*` paths | P1 | +31/-20 | Open |
| 5 | #7864 | Warn about SecretRefs, skills reload, WhatsApp re-pair | P1 | +37 | Open |
| 6 | #7868 | Provider api types, thinkingDefault enum, Matrix `accessToken` | P1 | +14/-8 | Open |
| 7 | #7862 | Handle TTS `edge` -> `microsoft` rename | P2 | +6/-5 | Open |

All independent, all single-file (`openclaw_to_hermes.py`), all against `main`.

### Pre-existing unmerged PRs (not by us)

| PR | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #4120 | `--include-sessions` for chat history import | Open, 0 reviews |
| #5639 | Agent profile migration docs | Open |
| #7280 | `claw cleanup` workflow docs | Open |

---

## 1. Confirmed Bugs (with PRs)

### 1a. Source files not found when workspace/ was renamed to workspace-main/ (P0)

**Root cause:** OpenClaw renamed `workspace/` to `workspace-main/` (and `workspace-{agentId}` for multi-agent). `source_candidate()` (line 615) only checks `workspace/` and `workspace.default/`. Users who upgraded OpenClaw before migrating have MEMORY.md, USER.md, SOUL.md, and skills in `workspace-main/` where the tool can't find them.

**Symptom:** "Memories not migrated", "agent has no context", "who am I?" returns blank post-migration. Most commonly reported migration failure.

**Fix:** #7869 — `source_candidate()` auto-checks `workspace-main/` and `workspace-assistant/` as fallbacks. Applies to all 12 source file lookups.

### 1b. `openclaw.json` orphaned after migration (P0)

**Code path:** `_offer_source_archival()` in `claw.py` (line 193) renames `~/.openclaw/` to `~/.openclaw.pre-migration-YYYYMMDD/`. `openclaw.json` goes with it. The `Migrator` class has no knowledge of the gateway config file.

**Symptom:** Gateway crashes with `ENOENT` or `unauthorized: gateway token missing`.

**Fix:** #5207 (pre-existing, 16 lines, unreviewed).

### 1c. API keys in `openclaw.json["env"]` invisible to migration (P0)

**Code path:** `load_openclaw_env()` (line 1108) reads only `~/.openclaw/.env`. The `openclaw.json` top-level `"env"` sub-object (and `"env.vars"`) is never parsed. Many setups store keys like `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` there.

**Symptom:** Keys silently missing. Provider calls fail at runtime.

**Fix:** #7860 — reads both `config["env"]` and `config["env"]["vars"]` as a fourth key source.

**References:** #4652, #4030, #1580

### 1d. Channel tokens not found at new OpenClaw paths (P1)

**Code path:** Platform-specific migration functions read tokens from flat paths (e.g. `channels.slack.botToken`). OpenClaw moved to `channels.slack.accounts.default.botToken`.

**Symptom:** Messaging platforms silently non-functional after migration.

**Fix:** #7861 — `_get_channel_field()` checks flat path first, then `accounts.default.*`.

**References:** #5191, #5190

### 1e. TTS config reads stale provider name (P2)

**Code path:** `migrate_tts_config()` reads `providers.edge`. OpenClaw renamed to `providers.microsoft`.

**Fix:** #7862

### 1f. Provider API type values and thinkingDefault enum drift (P1)

**Code path:** `migrate_full_providers()` maps `apiType` values `"openai"`, `"anthropic"`, `"cohere"`. OpenClaw now uses `"openai-completions"`, `"openai-responses"`, `"anthropic-messages"`, `"google-generative-ai"`. Similarly, `thinkingDefault` added `"minimal"`, `"xhigh"`, `"adaptive"` which were unmapped. Matrix uses `accessToken` not `botToken`.

**Fix:** #7868

### 1g. SecretRef file/exec sources silently dropped (P1)

**Code path:** `resolve_secret_input()` (line 326) returns `None` for file/exec-backed secrets. No warning recorded.

**Fix:** #7864

---

## 2. Potential improvements (no PR yet)

### 2a. Shared workspace pointer not isolated (P2)

`migrate_messaging_settings()` sets `MESSAGING_CWD` to the OpenClaw workspace path verbatim. Both Hermes and OpenClaw then point at the same directory. If the user later deletes `~/.openclaw/` and the workspace lived inside it, Hermes loses its workspace. The migration could copy workspace contents into a Hermes-owned directory instead of just pointing at the shared path.

Note: `_offer_source_archival()` mitigates this by offering to rename `~/.openclaw/` after migration, and in practice the workspace is often a user-controlled project directory outside `~/.openclaw/`.

### 2b. Multi-agent memory import (P2)

The migration could iterate `agents.list[].workspace` paths and at minimum offer to import their memories into separate files, or create Hermes profiles for each agent. Currently only the default agent's workspace is read; other agents' memories are silently left in the old directories (not merged or collapsed — just ignored).

---

## 3. Structural Gaps

### Missing migration support

- **Session history**: PR #4120 open since Mar 31, 0 reviews
- **Multi-agent setups**: Only the default agent migrates. Users with 3-8 agents report context loss. Archived to `agents-list.json` for manual recreation.
- **Cron jobs**: Archived, not migrated. No automated path to `hermes cron create`.
- **Gateway config**: Archived to `archive/gateway-config.json`. No settings (port, bind, auth) mapped to Hermes.
- **Session thread bindings**: Archived, not migrated.
- **Honcho/memory backend**: Backend config archived, no data migration.
- **Agent profiles**: PR #5639 documents manual workaround.
- **Hermes-to-hermes transfer**: No `hermes migrate export/import` for server moves.

### Missing post-migration safeguards

- **No verification step**: No `hermes claw verify` to check gateway starts, channels connect, keys resolve.
- **No auto-backup**: No snapshot before migration starts.
- **No idempotency**: Running twice produces unpredictable results.
- **No rollback**: No `--undo` mechanism.

---

## 4. OpenClaw Schema Changes the Tool Now Tracks

Comprehensive audit of the OpenClaw config schema (types, Zod validation, doctor migrations) against all 28 config-reading functions in the migration tool:

| Change | Migrate tool status |
|---|---|
| `workspace/` -> `workspace-main/` | **Fixed: #7869** |
| Channel tokens -> `accounts.default.*` | **Fixed: #7861** |
| TTS `edge` -> `microsoft` | **Fixed: #7862** |
| Provider `api` hyphenated values | **Fixed: #7868** |
| `thinkingDefault` new enum values | **Fixed: #7868** |
| Matrix `accessToken` field | **Fixed: #7868** |
| MCP servers at `mcp.servers` | Not drifted (still canonical path) |
| `talk.providers.*` with flat fallback | Not drifted (tool handles both) |
| All 28 config-reading functions null-safe | Confirmed (no KeyError risk) |

---

## 5. Community Impact

From ~180 community messages over two weeks:

- **Most common complaint**: Memories/persona not migrating (fixed by #7869)
- **Second**: API keys missing post-migration (fixed by #7860, #7861)
- **Third**: State confusion from leftover `~/.openclaw/` (needs better cleanup UX)
- **~30-40% positive reports**: Tool works well for simple single-agent setups with standard paths and keys in `.env`
- **Consistent pattern**: Users with complex/upgraded OpenClaw installs report fresh install + manual config produces better results than migration

items.body:
## Bug

The `suppressed_sources` field in `~/.hermes/auth.json` is written but never read by any code path. This means users cannot suppress auto-discovered credential sources (e.g. `claude_code` OAuth tokens from `~/.claude/.credentials.json`).

### Reproduction

1. Have a Claude Code OAuth token in `~/.claude/.credentials.json`
2. Add an Anthropic API key to the credential pool via `hermes auth`
3. Observe that `auth.json` contains:
   ```json
   "suppressed_sources": {
     "anthropic": ["claude_code"]
   }
   ```
4. Run `hermes chat` — the OAuth token is still injected into the pool and selected, causing a 400 error:
   ```
   "Third-party apps now draw from your extra usage, not your plan limits."
   ```

### Root cause

`_seed_from_singletons()` in `agent/credential_pool.py` (line ~975) unconditionally calls `read_claude_code_credentials()` and upserts the result into the pool. It never checks `suppressed_sources` from `auth.json`.

A grep for `suppressed_sources` across the entire Python codebase returns zero hits — the field is only present in the JSON file but no code reads or honors it.

### Expected behavior

`_seed_from_singletons()` should read `suppressed_sources` from `auth.json` and skip any source listed there. For example, if `suppressed_sources.anthropic` contains `"claude_code"`, the function should not upsert the `claude_code` entry.

### Workaround

Remove or rename `~/.claude/.credentials.json` so the OAuth token is not discovered:
```bash
mv ~/.claude/.credentials.json ~/.claude/.credentials.json.bak
```

### Environment

- hermes-agent v0.8.0 (2026.4.8), upstream af9caec4
- Arch Linux (NVIDIA GB10)
- Claude Code OAuth token present from prior `claude` CLI login

items.title: Support DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES for role-based access control
items.body:
## Feature Description

Allow Discord access control based on Discord roles (e.g., Moderator role) instead of hardcoded user IDs. Currently `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` only accepts a comma-separated list of user IDs, which requires manual updates when moderator ranks change.

## Motivation

Server moderation teams change frequently. Currently when a new moderator is added, someone must manually update `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` with their Discord user ID. This is error-prone and requires ongoing maintenance.

A role-based approach would let moderators self-serve: grant the role on the server, and access is automatic.

## Proposed Solution

Add a new environment variable `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` that accepts Discord role IDs:

```bash
DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES=1493705176387948674
DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS=413720629
```

Behavior:
1. If `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` is set, resolve the configured roles to members via the Discord API
2. Check if the message author has any of the allowed roles
3. Both `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` and `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` can coexist (union)
4. Resolved role memberships are cached and refreshed periodically (e.g., on gateway restart or on interval)

Implementation notes:
- Use Discord Guild API to resolve roles to member lists
- Placeholder for non-numeric entries in `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` already exists: `_resolve_allowed_usernames()`
- A similar `_resolve_allowed_roles()` method could follow the same pattern

## Alternatives Considered

- **Sync script** — Run an external cron job that syncs role members to `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS`. Works but adds operational complexity and a delay between granting role and granting access.
- **Bot mention + role check** — Keep current mention-based auth but check roles regardless of user ID. Doesn't solve the maintainability problem.

items.body:
## Summary

Cron jobs registered with `[SILENT] exec: bash script.sh` (script-only with no LLM judgment needed) still load the full `SOUL.md` / AGENTS.md context via `build_context_files_prompt()`, inflating token usage by 10-20k per run.

## Current behavior

In `cron/scheduler.py:705-728`, cron jobs create an `AIAgent` with:
- `skip_memory=True` ✅ (correctly excludes MEMORY.md / USER.md)
- `skip_context_files` is NOT set → defaults to False → **SOUL.md and context files are loaded**

For cron jobs that only run a shell script (`[SILENT] exec: ...`) and return `[SILENT]`, loading the agent's personality context is pure waste.

## Observed impact

Real metrics from a production install (30-min cron schedule):
- `memory-session-scan` (script-only): 63 sessions × ~30k tokens = ~1.9M tokens/7 days
- `memory-micro-cycle` (script-only): 32 sessions × ~30k tokens = ~1M tokens/7 days
- These tokens are pure context loading — the actual bash exec produces `[SILENT]`

For users on OpenAI Codex (ChatGPT Plus), this burns quota fast even when `model: gemini-3.1-flash-lite`.

## Proposed

Option A: Per-job flag in `jobs.json`:
```json
{
  "name": "memory-micro-cycle",
  "prompt": "[SILENT] exec: ...",
  "skip_context_files": true
}
```

Option B: Auto-detect "script-only" cron jobs (prompt starts with `[SILENT] exec:`) and skip context automatically.

Option C: Add a new job `kind` field like `"kind": "exec"` vs `"kind": "agent"`, where `exec` bypasses agent construction entirely and just runs the bash command.

Option C is the cleanest but biggest change. Option A is the minimal viable fix.

## Context

This affects users who migrated from OpenClaw-style file-based pipelines. OpenClaw's equivalent had zero LLM overhead for script-only tasks. Hermes cron's LLM-always-loaded design is one of the biggest cost surprises for that migration path (see NousResearch/hermes-agent#7481 for a related delegation fallback issue).

## Related files

- `cron/scheduler.py:705` — AIAgent construction in cron loop
- `run_agent.py:2815` — `skip_context_files` parameter usage
- `agent/prompt_builder.py:820` — context files loading
- `tools/delegate_tool.py:304` — already uses `skip_context_files=True` for subagents (precedent)

Subagents already have this handled correctly — cron should match.

items.title: [Bug]: Typing indicator missing in Telegram General topic for forum-enabled chats
items.body:
## Bug Description

In Telegram forum-enabled groups, `sendChatAction` (typing indicator) works in all topics **except** the General topic. The indicator silently fails because Telegram does not set `message_thread_id` on General-topic messages, and the gateway requires it for forum chats.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes gateway connected to Telegram
2. Create or use a group with forum topics enabled
3. Send a message in **any non-General topic** → typing indicator appears ✅
4. Send a message in the **General topic** → no typing indicator ❌

## Expected Behavior

Typing indicator should appear in all topics, including General.

## Actual Behavior

Typing indicator is missing in General topic only. No error is logged (failures are caught at debug level in `send_typing`).

## Root Cause Analysis

1. `telegram.py:2699` — `thread_id_raw = message.message_thread_id` → `None` for General topic (Telegram API omits it)
2. `telegram.py:2700` — `thread_id_str = str(thread_id_raw) if thread_id_raw else None` → `None`
3. `source.thread_id` is `None` at `telegram.py:2738`
4. `base.py:1461` — `_thread_metadata` becomes `None` (no `thread_id` to wrap)
5. `_keep_typing()` at `base.py:1163` calls `send_typing(chat_id, metadata=None)`
6. `telegram.py:1793` — `message_thread_id=None` passed to `send_chat_action`, which silently fails in forum-enabled chats

The `group_topics` config cannot help — it is gated behind `thread_id_str` being truthy (`telegram.py:2718`), so it never runs for General.

Additionally, the progress typing path has the same issue: `run.py:6651` sets `_progress_thread_id = source.thread_id` (None), so `_progress_metadata` is also None at `run.py:6652`.

**Note:** Community reports suggest `message_thread_id=1` for General may also fail with "message thread not found" (python-telegram-bot #4739), so the fix may need a fallback strategy.

## Proposed Fix

Detect forum-enabled groups when `message_thread_id` is absent and attempt to use the General topic thread ID. Two approaches:

1. In `_build_message_event`, detect forum groups (via `chat.is_forum`) and default `thread_id_str` to a known General topic ID when `message_thread_id` is None
2. In `send_typing`, if the chat is a forum and no `message_thread_id` is provided, try sending with a General topic fallback, catching "thread not found" errors gracefully

**Affected Component:** Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)
**Platform:** Telegram
**OS:** Ubuntu 24.04 (aarch64)
**Python:** 3.11
**Hermes Version:** 0.8.0

items.title: [Feature]: CerebroCortex memory provider — brain-analogous memory with associative networks, decay, and dream consolidation
items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

Hermes's built-in memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md) is great for pinned facts but limited to ~1,300 tokens with no semantic search, no decay model, and no automatic knowledge organization. The external memory providers help, but none combine all of: local-first storage, semantic search, associative linking, biologically-inspired decay, and multi-agent messaging.

Specific gaps in current memory options:

- No provider does associative graph search (finding related memories by traversing typed links, not just keyword/vector matching)
- No provider has memory decay — everything stays equally weighted forever until manually pruned
- No provider offers offline memory consolidation (pattern extraction, schema formation, automatic pruning of noise)
- Multi-agent memory sharing with agent-to-agent messaging isn't available in any current provider
- Several providers require cloud services or subscriptions; none are designed to run on minimal hardware like a Raspberry Pi

## Proposed Solution

Add [CerebroCortex](https://github.com/buckster123/CerebroCortex) as a memory provider plugin. It's an open-source (MIT), local-first AI memory system already published on PyPI as `cerebro-cortex`.

**What it brings:**

- **6 memory modalities** (episodic, semantic, procedural, affective, prospective, schematic) vs. flat text
- **Associative network with spreading activation** — memories link together via 9 typed/weighted link types, search finds related knowledge by traversing the graph
- **ACT-R + FSRS hybrid decay** — frequently-used memories stay sharp, unused ones fade naturally (power-law decay, not exponential)
- **Dream Engine** — LLM-powered offline consolidation that extracts patterns, forms abstractions, prunes noise, and discovers cross-domain connections
- **Multi-agent messaging** — send_message/check_inbox for agent-to-agent communication through shared memory
- **Triple-backend:** SQLite (graph) + ChromaDB (vectors) + igraph (traversal)
- **Runs on Raspberry Pi 5 (4GB)** — designed for minimal hardware

**Already working integration paths:**

1. **MCP server (works today, tested):** `pip install cerebro-cortex[mcp]`, add to config.yaml mcp_servers, get 46 tools as `mcp_cerebro_*`
2. **Memory provider plugin** (~200 lines of glue code): would add prefetch, sync_turn, and system_prompt_block hooks for automatic enrichment
3. **REST API** on port 8767 for cross-device agent sharing

I've tested option 1 on a fresh Hermes install (Pi 5, Claude Opus 4). All 46 MCP tools registered, remember/recall/associate/messaging all working. Sub-second response times. Auto-linking creates semantic connections between stored memories without manual intervention.

**Detailed integration report with architecture comparison:**

items.title: is_local_endpoint misses Docker/Podman DNS names — stale timeout fires on local LLM proxies

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

`is_local_endpoint()` in `agent/model_metadata.py` only matches IP addresses, `localhost`, and `_LOCAL_HOSTS`. When running Hermes behind a local LLM proxy (e.g. LiteLLM, Ollama) accessed via Docker/Podman DNS name (like `hermes-litellm` or `ollama`), the function returns `False`.

This causes the stale stream timeout (180s default) to NOT be auto-disabled (the fix from #6368), leading to the infinite retry loop described in #7069 — the local model is still prefilling but the agent kills the connection and reconnects.

## Root Cause

The check at line ~4951 in `run_agent.py`:
```python
if _stream_stale_timeout_base == 180.0 and self.base_url and is_local_endpoint(self.base_url):
    _stream_stale_timeout = float("inf")
```

...never triggers because `is_local_endpoint("http://hermes-litellm:4000/v1")` returns `False` — it's not an IP, not in `_LOCAL_HOSTS`, and the hostname can't be parsed as an IP address.

## Proposed Fix

Three additions to `is_local_endpoint()`:

1. **Unqualified hostnames (no dots)** → always local. A hostname like `ollama`, `litellm`, or `hermes-litellm` is always a local network name (Docker DNS, mDNS, /etc/hosts). This covers the most common case with zero configuration.

2. **DNS resolution fallback** — resolve the hostname to an IP with `socket.gethostbyname()`, then check if it's private. This catches qualified local hostnames like `ollama.local` or `litellm.internal`.

3. **Configurable `model.local_endpoints`** — a list of hostnames in config.yaml to explicitly mark as local. Useful for edge cases where DNS resolution isn't available or the hostname is unusual.

## Related

- #7069 — Infinite retry loop caused by stream stale timeout during local LLM prefill phase
- #6368 — fix: disable stale stream timeout for local providers (merged, but incomplete for Docker DNS)

items.title: hermes claw migrate should warn if OpenClaw is still running
items.body:
## Problem

When `hermes claw migrate` copies Telegram (or Discord/Slack) bot tokens from the OpenClaw config, both Hermes and OpenClaw end up using the same token simultaneously. Telegram only allows one active session per bot token — the second process kicks the first off. This breaks messaging for both until one is stopped.

Users report this as "migration broke my Telegram" when the actual fix is just stopping OpenClaw before starting Hermes.

## Suggestion

Add a check before migration runs that warns if an OpenClaw process is detected (e.g. gateway, node process with openclaw in the command line). Something like:

> ⚠ OpenClaw appears to be running. Messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack) only allow one active connection per bot token. Stop OpenClaw before migrating to avoid conflicts.

This could be a warning that the user can override, not a hard block.

## Context

This was the most common co-location complaint in the community Discord during the Mar 28 - Apr 11 migration wave. Multiple users described Telegram "breaking" after migration when both were running on the same machine.

items.body:
Title: Matrix gateway can send messages but doesn't receive/respond to incoming messages (mautrix client started incorrectly)

Summary
The Matrix gateway can successfully authenticate and send messages, and logs show initial sync + joined rooms, but it never processes incoming room messages (no replies). Root cause appears to be that the adapter runs manual `client.sync()` calls without starting the mautrix client's event dispatcher, so `add_event_handler(...)` callbacks are never invoked.

Environment
- Hermes Agent gateway Matrix adapter
- mautrix installed (`mautrix[encryption]`)
- Using access token auth
- Non-encrypted rooms (also reproduces in DM)

Reproduction
1. Configure Matrix env vars:
   - MATRIX_HOMESERVER=https://<homeserver>
   - MATRIX_USER_ID=@<bot>:<server>
   - MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN=<token>
2. Start gateway
3. Send a message to the bot in a DM / room where the bot is joined

Observed
- Bot can send messages (e.g., gateway-initiated notices succeed)
- Logs show e.g.:
  - "Matrix: using access token for ..."
  - "Matrix: initial sync complete, joined N rooms"
- But bot never replies to user messages
- No handler logs such as `_on_room_message` / `handle_message` are triggered

Expected
- Incoming Matrix `m.room.message` events should invoke registered handlers and feed the gateway message pipeline.

Root cause (hypothesis)
The adapter registers event handlers with `client.add_event_handler(...)`, but only runs `await client.sync(...)` in a custom loop.
In mautrix, event handlers are dispatched by the client's internal syncer started via `client.start(...)` (and stopped via `client.stop()`). Manual `client.sync()` does not dispatch the event handlers.

Proposed fix (minimal)
In `gateway/platforms/matrix.py`:
- After successful auth and handler registration, start the client syncer:
  - `self._client.start(None)`
- On disconnect, stop it:
  - `self._client.stop()`
- Keep the existing periodic loop only for lightweight maintenance (refresh joined room IDs, crypto key share, retry decryptions), but do not rely on it for event dispatch.

Impact
Without this, Matrix gateway appears "connected" but is effectively one-way (outbound only), which blocks DM / room interaction.

Notes
I verified on a real homeserver that adding `client.start(None)` immediately enables replies; the bot began receiving and responding to DM messages.

Telegram users can receive internal Hermes system/status messages as if they were normal chat messages. In my case this happened with two separate strings:

1. `📬 No home channel is set for Telegram. A home channel is where Hermes delivers cron job results and cross-platform messages.`
2. `Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (4.9s elapsed).`

This appears to be two related UX/runtime issues:
- the gateway proactively sends a Telegram home-channel setup prompt into the DM when `TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL` is unset
- interruption handling can surface `Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (...)` back into the visible chat instead of keeping it internal / converting it into a friendlier message / queueing the new message cleanly

## Environment
- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Commit: `0848a79476e5fe52354287a93ef48f262908127c`
- Branch: `main`

items.title: [Bug] Queued voice-message STT speech-to-text regression in gateway
items.body:
## Summary
Queued/interrupted voice messages lose speech-to-text transcription in the gateway.

When a voice note arrives while a session is already busy, the adapter correctly queues a full `MessageEvent` with cached audio metadata, but the gateway later dequeues it through a text-only helper that flattens the event into a placeholder string. That destroys the audio metadata before the follow-up re-enters the normal inbound preprocessing path, so STT never runs.

This makes the bug look like “Hermes is not receiving my voice messages,” even though:
- Telegram voice caching works
- the configured STT backend works
- manual transcription of the cached `.ogg` succeeds

## Root cause
The queued follow-up path in `gateway/run.py` uses `_dequeue_pending_text()` and turns media-only events into text like:

`[User sent audio: /path/to/file.ogg]`

That bypasses the normal `_enrich_message_with_transcription()` path used by `_handle_message_with_agent()`.

## CGC-traced flow
1. `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` caches voice notes into `event.media_urls` / `event.media_types`
2. `gateway/run.py:_handle_message_with_agent()` normally detects audio and runs STT
3. `gateway/platforms/base.py` queues non-photo follow-ups as full `MessageEvent` objects while a session is active
4. `gateway/run.py:_run_agent()` dequeues those follow-ups through a text-only helper
5. queued voice notes skip STT entirely

## Expected behavior
Queued/interrupted voice follow-ups should preserve the full `MessageEvent` and re-enter the same inbound preprocessing pipeline as normal messages, so STT runs regardless of whether the voice note was first-in-turn or queued while the agent was busy.

## Acceptance criteria
- queued voice events keep their `media_urls` / `media_types`
- queued follow-ups reuse the same inbound preprocessing used by normal messages
- queued voice notes are transcribed through `_enrich_message_with_transcription()`
- regression tests cover queued voice-event dequeue + transcription behavior

## Scope
This issue is specifically an STT speech-to-text bug in queued/interrupted voice-message handling.

items.body:
## Summary

Extends the per-task model parameter from #7586 with **named tiers** and a **model discovery tool**, so the agent can make informed delegation decisions without knowing deployment-specific model identifiers.

## Motivation

With #7586, the agent can pass `model="google/gemini-flash-2.0"` to `delegate_task`. But:
- The agent needs to know exact model names for the deployment
- Different users have different models available
- The agent has no way to discover what's available at runtime

This is the complementary piece: **tiers abstract model names**, and **list_models lets the agent discover what's available**.

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Model Tiers (`delegation.model_tiers`)

```yaml
delegation:
  model_tiers:
    small: google/gemini-flash-2.0     # fast/cheap
    # medium: omit to inherit parent model
    large: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6   # complex reasoning
```

The agent can then say:
```python
delegate_task(goal="List all .py files", model="small")        # → gemini flash
delegate_task(goal="Review this PR for security", model="large") # → opus
delegate_task(goal="Debug the auth flow")                        # → parent model (medium)
```

Tier names resolve to configured model names. Unknown tiers fall back to the parent model.

### 2. `list_models` Tool

Returns available models with tier assignments, context lengths, and providers:

```json
{
  "models": [
    {"name": "qwen35-397b", "provider": "litellm", "context_length": 524288, "is_default": true},
    {"name": "gemma4-nothink", "provider": "litellm", "context_length": 262144, "tier": "small"},
    {"name": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "provider": "litellm", "context_length": 1000000, "tier": "large"}
  ],
  "tiers": {"small": "gemma4-nothink", "large": "claude-sonnet-4-6"},
  "default_model": "qwen35-397b"
}
```

Registered in the `delegation` toolset alongside `delegate_task`.

### Use Cases

- **Explorer subagent**: `delegate_task(goal="Find all files related to auth", model="small")` — fast file discovery on a cheap model
- **Peer review**: `delegate_task(goal="Review my implementation", model="large")` — escalate to a stronger model
- **Mixed batch**: different model per task based on complexity
- **Self-awareness**: agent calls `list_models` to discover what's available before deciding

### Why This Is Better Than smart_model_routing

We deployed and tested `smart_model_routing` (message-length heuristic) in production and disabled it (see #7905). Short messages like "yes" or "go ahead" can trigger the most complex operations — message length is a terrible proxy for task complexity.

**Model-directed delegation is fundamentally better**: the model has full context, knows the task complexity, and chooses the right model for each subagent. No heuristics, no false positives.

### Relationship to Other PRs

- **#7586** (Labhund) — foundation: per-task model parameter on delegate_task. This PR builds on top.
- **#7201** — named routing profiles. Complementary but orthogonal — profiles are about predefined route bundles, tiers are about simple capability labels.
- **#7905** — our issue about `is_local_endpoint` + smart routing concerns.

### Implementation

We have a working implementation on our fork. Happy to submit a PR once #7586 lands, or rebase on top of it.

Credit: Per-task model parameter design from @Labhund (#7586). Tier + list_models additions from our production deployment.

items.title: Streaming mode breaks reply_to_mode for Telegram/Discord
items.body:
## Bug Description

When streaming is enabled (`streaming.enabled: true`), the `reply_to_mode` setting (off/first/all) does not work for Telegram (and likely Discord). Replies are never threaded to the user's original message.

## Root Cause

The `GatewayStreamConsumer` class in `gateway/stream_consumer.py` does not receive or use the `reply_to` parameter:

1. `GatewayStreamConsumer.__init__` has no `reply_to` parameter
2. `_send_new_chunk` method has a `reply_to_id` parameter but always receives `None` because the consumer is never initialized with the original message ID
3. In `gateway/run.py` (around line 7399-7404), the stream consumer is created without passing the event message ID:

```python
_stream_consumer = GatewayStreamConsumer(
    adapter=_adapter,
    chat_id=source.chat_id,
    config=_consumer_cfg,
    metadata={"thread_id": _progress_thread_id} if _progress_thread_id else None,
)
```

## Expected Behavior

When `reply_to_mode: all` is set via environment variable `TELEGRAM_REPLY_TO_MODE=all` or in config.yaml, all streaming message chunks should be threaded/reply to the user's original message.

## Workaround

Disable streaming:
```yaml
streaming:
  enabled: false
```

## Suggested Fix

1. Add `reply_to: Optional[str] = None` parameter to `GatewayStreamConsumer.__init__`
2. Store it as `self._reply_to`
3. Pass it to `_send_new_chunk` calls (respect the `reply_to_mode` setting: first chunk only for `first` mode, all chunks for `all` mode)
4. In `gateway/run.py`, pass `event.message_id` when creating the stream consumer

## Environment

- Platform: Telegram (likely affects Discord too based on similar adapter pattern)
- Config: `TELEGRAM_REPLY_TO_MODE=all` + `streaming.enabled: true`
