## Problem

Tool schemas are ~8.7K tokens per request (#4379) — 46% of the 12.5K baseline. `hermes tools disable` exists but is global: disabling a tool removes it from every session, every profile.

For a casual chat or a quick question, the model doesn't need browser_click, web_crawl, delegate_task, or vision tools. But there's no way to say "this profile only needs memory + files + terminal" without permanently disabling tools for all other profiles too.

Community users are manually building tool indexes to work around this — replacing full schemas with one-line summaries and only loading the full definition on demand. This is the same pattern skills already use (each skill is ~10-20 tokens in the system prompt, expanded only when invoked).

## Proposal

Extend `hermes tools` to support per-profile tool selection. Something like:

```yaml
# In profile config or config.yaml
profiles:
  chat:
    tools: [memory, read_file, bash, web_search]
  coding:
    tools: [memory, read_file, write_file, bash, python, git]
  full:
    tools: all  # current default behavior
```

Or via CLI:

```
hermes tools enable memory read_file bash --profile chat
hermes tools enable all --profile coding
```

The default profile would keep `tools: all` (no behavior change for existing users). Users who want a leaner baseline can create a profile with a reduced toolset.

## Impact

| Toolset | Estimated tokens | Savings vs default |
|---------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Full (31 tools, current default) | ~8,700 | — |
| Coding (10 tools) | ~2,800 | ~5,900 (68%) |
| Chat (5 tools) | ~1,400 | ~7,300 (84%) |

On cached providers (Anthropic, OpenAI), the savings apply to the first call per cache window. On local models, the savings apply to every call and also reduce latency significantly (tool-formatted prompts are 10x slower to process than plain text per #6839).

## Prior art

- `hermes tools disable` — global tool toggle, already exists
- Skills use a lightweight index pattern (name + one-line description, ~10-20 tokens each, full skill expanded on demand)
- #6839 proposes lazy tool loading as an alternative approach

## Notes

- This doesn't change defaults — `tools: all` remains the default
- Profiles already exist as a concept in Hermes (`hermes profiles`)
- The tool registry (`tools/registry.py`) already has per-tool metadata that could support filtering

items.title: [Feature] Toolset-level enable/disable in config
items.body:
## Problem

`hermes tools disable` works per-tool, but with 31+ tools it's tedious to configure a lean setup. Tools already have a `toolset` field in the registry (file, browser, web, terminal, memory, vision, delegate, etc.) but there's no way to enable/disable at the toolset level.

## Proposal

Add `tools.toolsets` to `config.yaml`:

```yaml
tools:
  toolsets:
    - file
    - terminal
    - memory
    - web
```

When set, only tools belonging to the listed toolsets are loaded. When omitted (default), all toolsets load as today.

This is simpler than per-profile tool selection (#7961) and works with the existing registry infrastructure — `ToolEntry` already has a `toolset` field, and `ToolRegistry` already tracks toolset membership. The filtering would go in `get_enabled_tools()` or equivalent.

## Examples

| Use case | Toolsets | Approx tools | Approx tokens |
|----------|---------|-------------|--------------|
| Chat / Q&A | memory | ~3 | ~800 |
| Coding | file, terminal, memory | ~8 | ~2,500 |
| Research | file, web, memory | ~8 | ~2,500 |
| Full (current default) | all | ~31 | ~8,700 |

## Relation to other issues

- Complements #7961 (per-profile tool selection) — this is the simpler global version
- Reduces the same 8.7K overhead as #6839 (lazy loading) without API workarounds
- The registry already groups tools by toolset — this just exposes the grouping to config

items.title: [Docs] docker.md missing local LLM connection guide (host.docker.internal)
items.body:
## Problem

PR #7950 added Docker/Podman/Lima DNS name detection to `is_local_endpoint()` — these hostnames now auto-trigger relaxed streaming timeouts. But the docs don't mention this anywhere:

- **docker.md** has no section about connecting to a host-side LLM (Ollama, llama.cpp, etc.) from inside a Hermes container
- **local-llm-on-mac.md** Timeouts section says "localhost, LAN IPs" but doesn't mention `host.docker.internal` and friends

## User impact

A user running Hermes in Docker + Ollama on the host has no docs guidance on:
1. Which hostname to use (`host.docker.internal` vs `localhost` — the latter won't work from inside Docker)
2. That Hermes auto-detects these hostnames as local (no manual timeout config needed)

## Proposed fix

1. Add a "Connecting to local LLMs on the host" section to `docker.md` with a hostname table (Docker/Podman/Lima) and a config example
2. Update the auto-detection description in `local-llm-on-mac.md` Timeouts section to mention container DNS names
